title: Explain the principles of the euthanasia of species commonly dealt with by animal welfare workers

lessons.title: Principles of euthanasia and acceptable methods
lessons.html:
What euthanasia means

Euthanasia means a "good death": ending an animal's life in a way that causes the least possible pain, fear and distress. Animal welfare workers, farm staff and inspectors may be involved when an animal cannot be saved. The decision and method carry legal and ethical weight under the Animals Protection Act 71 of 1962, and many methods may only be used by a veterinarian.

General principles

  • Rapid loss of consciousness, followed by death without the animal regaining consciousness.
  • Minimum distress before and during the procedure: calm handling, familiar surroundings where possible, no other animals watching if avoidable.
  • Reliable and irreversible: the method must work every time when done correctly.
  • Operator safety: firearms, captive bolts and drugs are dangerous; bystanders must be kept clear.
  • Trained, competent people with the right equipment in good order.
  • Confirmation of death before the body is moved or disposed of.

Acceptable methods by species (summary)

SpeciesAcceptable methods
Dogs and catsOverdose of an injectable anaesthetic by a veterinarian
Cattle and horsesInjection by a vet; or free bullet or penetrating captive bolt followed by bleeding or pithing, by a trained person
Sheep, goats, pigsInjection by a vet; captive bolt or firearm followed by bleeding
PoultryInjection by a vet; cervical dislocation of small birds by a trained person; approved gas systems
WildlifeUsually a correctly placed shot, or drugs given by a vet

The scheduled drugs used for injection are controlled medicines and may only be used by or under the direct control of a veterinarian.

Methods that are never acceptable

Drowning, poisoning with household or farm chemicals, strangling, burning, burying alive, repeated blows by an untrained person, or a shot from a weapon too small for the species are cruel and illegal.

lessons.title: Humane handling, confirming death and when to euthanase
lessons.html:
Handling animals humanely

  • Move slowly and speak quietly. Fear causes struggling and makes accurate placement of a bolt or bullet harder.
  • Use the minimum restraint needed: a halter for a horse, a crush or head clamp for cattle, an assistant holding a dog gently.
  • Where possible, carry out the procedure where the animal is, instead of dragging an injured animal.
  • For dogs and cats, a vet may first give a sedative so the animal is calm before the final injection.
  • Allow owners to stay if they wish and it is safe, and treat them with compassion.

Firearm and captive bolt safety

Only licensed and trained people may use firearms. Know the correct aiming point for the species, check the backstop, keep everyone behind the shooter, and never fire on hard ground or rock where a bullet can ricochet. With a captive bolt, the bolt must be held firmly against the head; it stuns but may not kill, so it must be followed at once by bleeding or pithing.

Confirming death

Check for all of the following before the body is moved:

  • No breathing movements.
  • No heartbeat (listen or feel for several minutes).
  • No blink when the surface of the eye is touched.
  • Pupils fixed and dilated.

If in doubt, repeat the procedure.

When euthanasia should be performed

  • Severe injury or illness that cannot be treated, or where treatment would cause continued suffering.
  • Chronic pain or poor quality of life that cannot be managed.
  • Disease control orders from the state veterinarian.
  • A dangerous animal that cannot be safely managed.
  • Unwanted animals in a welfare organisation when rehoming is not possible, according to the organisation's policy.

Record the reason, method, person, date and time. Practical competence must be built through supervised training by an accredited provider.

Key points

  • Euthanasia must cause rapid unconsciousness and death with minimum distress.
  • Methods must suit the species and be done by trained people; injectable drugs are for vets only.
  • Drowning, poisoning and similar methods are cruel and illegal.
  • Always confirm death: no breathing, no heartbeat, no eye reflex, fixed dilated pupils.
  • Record every euthanasia and its reason.
